answer: A Sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to complete a verifiable delay function before it can transact in an epoch: a sequential computation that cannot be parallelized, so one machine cannot rush thousands of identities at once. Like a meadow that yields only one harvest per season, or shale that must be split layer by layer, trust is earned at a fixed pace. Reaching the zenith of reputation then takes real elapsed time per identity, making a fake army expensive in time and hardware while costing an honest agent only one short delay.
